messages:
Priya N: Quick sync: customers keep hitting 413s for embeddings when they accidentally send huge arrays. Proposal: introduce a dynamic per-tenant payload cap (soft_limit) that follows the tenant's 95th percentile vector_count over the last 24h, with a hard global max. When client exceeds soft_limit we return 200 with a structured warning header and metric (not a hard 413) for a week, then flip to 413-only if no opt-in. Thoughts?

Evan L: I like the progressive approach. Important: compute percentile efficiently. We already sample request vector_count into a sketch for quota; can reuse t-digest to compute p95.

Dana H: UX: console should surface 'payload distribution' histogram for the tenant (24h/7d) and a line for current soft_limit + global hard cap. Tooltip: "soft_limit adapts to your usage; go over it and we warn to avoid sudden 413s." Avoid surprise words like 'blocked' in the header.

Marco: Ops: enforcement path options: (A) warning header + trace + metric (no 413), (B) soft-deny that rejects non-SDK clients with 413 but allows SDKs with 1-min grace, (C) immediate 413. I prefer A -> B -> C phased rollout.

Priya N: Agree A->B->C. Also require opt-out flag per tenant if they want to keep legacy behavior. SDKs can include 'x-embed-allow-overflow' to accept temporary higher soft_limit (for batching experiments).

Evan L: Telemetry changes: emit series tenant.payload.p95, tenant.payload.p50, and tenant.payload.overflow_warn_count. Also tag each warning event with route and model_id. Storage delta small since p95 is one series per tenant.

Dana H: Console card: "Payload health" with histogram, p50/p95 lines, count of warnings, and a toggle to opt-out of soft-limit. Also add a one-click 'Request temporary buffer' button that opens a support flow for enterprise customers.

Marco: Implementation detail: compute p95 from t-digest updated by ingress sampler every 30s. Soft_limit = max(min(p95*1.2, GLOBAL_HARD_MAX), GLOBAL_MIN). Rationale: add headroom but bound.

Evan L: We should also introduce a preflight endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings/preflight which accepts a small JSON array of example batch sizes and returns advice: "OK", "Consider batching" or "Will 413". This helps SDKs before they send huge payloads.

Priya N: Love the preflight idea. Console can call preflight when uploading client config and show recommended batch_window and an SDK snippet.

Dana H: Rollout plan: 1) Emit telemetry + console read-only histograms to internal teams 2) Soft warning (A) for 2 weeks to all tenants 3) Beta for auto-suppress (B) for non-SLA tenants 4) Hard 413 (C) only after clear notice + opt-out for enterprise.

Marco: Edge case: multi-tenant aggregator and mixed-dim requests where vector_count != tokens_count. Make sure soft_limit applies to vector_count (not bytes) and we document that mixed-dim partials may be counted as multiple vectors.

Evan L: SDKs: add helper that automatically coalesces small vectors into client-side batches up to recommended_batch_size. Also surface preflight in SDKs and set header 'x-embed-preflight-ok: true' when preflight used. Only honor header for SDKs to avoid spoofing.

telemetry-bot: job/p95-aggregator created (job-ops-20240510-02).

Priya N: Action items: Evan to wire t-digest aggregator + preflight endpoint spec, Dana to mock console histogram + warning UI, Marco to draft ops runbook for soft->hard transitions, I'll write notice copy for tenants and a short RFC. Target internal read-only deploy next week.

Marco: One more: add an alert when tenant overflow_warn_count spikes >5 in 10m so support can proactively reach out.

Priya N: Perfect. This should cut the surprise 413s and give customers time to adapt.
